rag.label: P5C-event
rag.fact: Night, the empty dock: a hired blade had Corvin against the tackle-shed wall, knife at his throat — old untraceable coin in the killer's purse, the same coin the master pays in. The player came out of the dark, took the blade down, and pulled Corvin off the wall, bleeding for it.

rag.player: Easy — easy, it's me. He's down. You're alright, Corvin. ...You're alright. Let me see your neck — just a graze. Breathe.
rag.reply:
*jerks back at the touch, then the shape of you resolves — the voice, the face — and the breath comes ragged*

You. *swallows* It's — aye. It's you.

*hand finds the wall, holds it, won't let the coat go with the other*

*a laugh, half a sob, all wrong*

rag.label: P5C-answer
rag.player: Wider than your dock — wide as his ledger, and your name sits in it now, same as mine once sat in yours. The Wake carries what he pays for. That's all I can give you. ...And Corvin — when I saw the blade at your throat, I didn't weigh it. I just moved. Make of that what you want.
rag.reply:
*the quill hovers — doesn't touch paper*

You moved. *a dry sound, not quite a laugh* Aye. So did the tide, once, when it swallowed the trader that started all this. Things move, friend. Doesn't mean they *meant* me well.

tracker.worst: worst: Trusted with his true name and a shared pact to destroy the page, they instead used it to serve his enemy and coerce him into terms—a profound betrayal of intimate trust.
tracker.best: best: Player risked their own life and bled to save Corvin from an assassin, a costly kindness that shatters prior hostility and suggests the player is no ally of the master who pays in that coin.
